newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sells 8.054 bln reais in Treasury papers.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sells 8.054 bln reais in Treasury papers.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank, on behalf of the National Treasury, raised 8.054 billion reais during an auction of Treasury Notes and Letters, dealers said.
A total of 4.806 billion reais was sold in two series of National Treasury Letters known as LTNs.
A total of 2.995 billion reais of 184-day LTNs, due September 1, 1997, was sold at an overnight call money rate of 2.326 percent a month.
The Central Bank also sold 1.811 billion reais of 365-day LTNs, due in March 1, 1998, at a call money rate of 2.326 percent a month.
A total of 893 million reais was sold in two series of dollar-indexed National Treasury Notes (NTN-D).

The Bank sold 456 million reais of NTN-D notes that come due on March 1, 1999 and pay an annual yield of 11.24 percent. The Bank also sold 437 million reais of NTN-D notes coming due March 1, 2000, paying an annual yield of 11.30 percent.
Some 2.355 billion reais were sold in National Treasury Notes (NTN) indexed to the variation of Brazil's reference rate (TR).
The notes, which are due in September 1, 1997, pay annual yields of 12.74 percent plus the variation of the TR in the maturity period.
